title: Check yourself: What the SDK does for you, and a raw client

questions.stem: Verbose diagnostics are on in a deployed service. Credentials look masked in the output, but customers' messages show up in it. What should the team do?

options.text: Keep it on, because the SDK masks sensitive data in request and response bodies
options.says: Ruled out because "sensitive data in request and response bodies may still be visible".

options.text: Switch that mode off for live traffic and record request ids instead
options.says: The page says that "customer text does not belong in a log by default", and request ids are the safe handle for a support ticket.

options.text: Redact the headers further so that the output holds no credentials at all
options.says: Ruled out because "headers are partly redacted, bodies are not", and the leak is in the bodies.

options.text: Log only the failing calls so that less customer text reaches the output
options.says: Ruled out because failing calls carry customer text too, and "customer text does not belong in a log by default".

questions.stem: A service sets nothing on its SDK client and calls the API in a month where the organisation has already reached its monthly spend cap. What happens to each call?

options.text: It is attempted once, because the SDK reads the cap and stops early
options.says: Ruled out because "two retries is a default for a generic caller" and the SDK does not inspect the cap.

options.text: It is attempted once, because a 429 is never retried by the SDK
options.says: Ruled out because "certain errors are automatically retried 2 times by default".

options.text: It is attempted three times, and the third attempt succeeds after a pause
options.says: Ruled out because the cap "stays in force until the next month begins", so no pause helps.

options.text: It is attempted three times in all, and every attempt fails
options.says: Two retries after the first attempt make three, and a spend-cap 429 "stays in force until the next month begins".
